name: What are the most common mistakes homeowners make?

mainEntity.name: What do people get wrong most often when converting a garage to living space?
mainEntity.text: What do people get wrong most often when converting a garage to living space?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common mistake is treating the garage like a simple interior remodel. In reality, a conversion touches structure, energy performance, utilities, and habitability all at once. Homeowners often start with a floor plan before confirming slab condition, ceiling height, roof framing, electrical capacity, or drainage. That leads to expensive redesigns. Another frequent error is underestimating the importance of insulation, air sealing, and sound control, which makes the finished room uncomfortable. People also sometimes ignore how the loss of garage function affects parking, storage, and daily convenience. On the permitting side, vague scope descriptions and incomplete drawings can create avoidable plan check corrections. The best protection is a feasibility-first approach: inspect the existing garage, define the end use, estimate utility upgrades, and only then finalize the layout. A good contractor should help identify hidden risks early so the project budget reflects reality. When the upfront planning is strong, the conversion is much more likely to feel like a real upgrade rather than a compromised afterthought.
acceptedAnswer.description: The biggest mistakes are skipping feasibility checks, underestimating permit requirements, ignoring insulation and moisture issues, and designing a layout before confirming the structure can support it. These mistakes usually lead to delays, change orders, and a space that feels unfinished.
